attempted_claim: Let Gamma_d, d>=3, be the Dani-Thomas sequence of defining graphs (Figure 7 of Dani-Naqvi-Soroko-Thomas, arXiv:2209.15254) with right-angled Coxeter group W_{Gamma_d} of divergence ≃ r^d and hypergraph index d-1. Let (W_{Gamma_d})_2(m,n) be its (m,n)-duplex per Definition 5.1, with m>=3 odd and 5<=n<infinity. Prove, up to ≃-equivalence of divergence functions, that Div((W_{Gamma_d})_2(m,n)) ≃ r^d, i.e. prove the lower bound Div ≽ r^d (the upper bound Div ≼ r^d follows from Theorem 1.4(3) since h=d-1).
decisive_failure: The r^d lower bound for odd-m finite-n duplexes remains open: proving it needs a new odd-fiber wall calculus, a new finite-label geodesic-ray construction, and rebuilt separation lemmas, which is a new-paper-scale program beyond this pass; the supporting dihedral computation covers only the I_2(m) local models, not the full Davis-complex geometry.
